key_concepts: Matter has two broad classes: substances and mixtures.
Pure substances are homogeneous with uniform composition and appearance.
Mixtures can be homogeneous or heterogeneous.
Mixtures can be separated by physical techniques such as evaporation, distillation, and fi
Components of pure substances are chemically combined and difficult to separate.
Water is a pure substance made of hydrogen and oxygen and can be separated by electrolysis
Pure substances have fixed sharp boiling and melting temperatures.
During boiling, a pure substance's temperature becomes constant after an initial change.
A pure substance melts completely and smoothly within a short time, while a mixture may no
Testing boiling point or melting point helps distinguish pure substances from mixtures.
A solution is a homogeneous mixture.
Examples of pure substances include oxygen, water, gold, carbon dioxide, and carbon.
